decisions.source_text: **first-principles bic derivation under coordinate change yields a jacobian coefficient of −2, not +1 (v1.1) or −1 (v1.2). three sequential patches each had a math error because the formula was bic-by-convention with retrofitted patches, not derived from a stated likelihood axiom.** the recursive audit (gp153 iters 0-1) cross-validated by independent o3 mutators with --dynamic=1 committee rotation showed both v1.1 and v1.2 retain a residual n·ln\ c\ frame-invariance bias under `h_out → c·h_out`. correct derivation: nll_framed = (n/2)·log(2π σ̂²_y') + n/2 − σ log\ h'(y_i)\ ; bic = 2·nll + k·log n gives n·log σ̂² **− 2·σ log\ h'\ ** + k·log n. under c-scaling, σ̂²·c² contributes +2n·log\ c\ in term 1; jacobian's `−2 σ log(c·h')` contributes −2n·log\ c\ in term 2; cancel exactly. v1.3 corrects coefficient to −2; verified frame-invariance pre-implementation via `scripts/verify_v1_3_frame_invariance.py` (drift < 1 bit across c ∈ {0.1, 0.5, 1, 2, 10}). **methodological lesson:** when a formula needs a third patch, stop patching — derive from first principles. three patch cycles is the cycle-detector for "bic-by-convention is wrong here." `confirmed / cross-llm-validated / first-principles-derived` spec v1.3 ships with mathematically-correct mdl. v2.0 (nml / stochastic complexity / pre-quantized coding) queued as research project for heteroscedastic + low-precision regimes that v1.3 honestly excludes. the "stop patching, start deriving" rule is a candidate methodology guideline for any specification that needs a third patch in a row. `projects/gp153_framer_spec_critique/champion_eval_results.json`, `research_areas/private/specs/active/gp-152_framer_architecture_spec_v1_3.md` (tbd), `scripts/verify_v1_3_frame_invariance.py` (tbd)

Correct derivation: NLL_framed = (N/2)·log(2π σ̂²_y') + N/2 − Σ log\|h'(y_i)\|; BIC = 2·NLL + K·log N gives N·log σ̂² **− 2·Σ log\|h'\|** + K·log N. decisions.source_text: **held-out failure in a fit-and-verify system arises from (at least) three distinct mechanisms, which residuals alone cannot distinguish:** (a) *variance underdetermination* — many parameter settings fit visible equally well, detectable by high bootstrap std; (b) *specification error from truncated support* — visible slice's loss minimum is systematically biased away from the full-data minimum, bootstrap converges tightly to the wrong answer, detectable by residual/std ratio >> 1; (c) *vocabulary failure* — indistinguishable from (b) by bootstrap alone, requires a one-time operator-level tail-supervised probe on the family. gp-023's sandbox_05 stretched-exp failure was case (b), confirmed by three probes: oracle test (visible-only loss → fails), tail-supervised oracle test (rules out vocabulary), bootstrap identifiability (rules out variance, confirms bias). the correct architectural upgrade is a **three-layer identifiability guard** in the fitter contract: bootstrap std + extrapolation spread + residual/std ratio — none of which require held-out labels. the correct project-level fix for gp-023 is to expand the visible slice (not tail-data injection, not sp-2, not gp-047 preservation-lane). `high / generalizable / three-probe stack` three different things look the same (wrong answer) but need different fixes; you need three tests to tell them apart e-gp023-ot-01 (visible-only, no pass), e-gp023-ot-02 (tail-supervised, λ=1 passes → rules out vocab), e-gp023-ot-03 (bootstrap, max_std 0.00741, ratio 2.85 → confirms bias not variance) `research_areas/private/seams/gp-023_ontology_trap_planck_mechanism_seam.md` turns 36–39, `workspace/identifiability_diagnostic_results.json`, `workspace/oracle_test_tail_supervised_results.json`

decisions.source_text: **open-ended scientific discovery under ztare is possible in principle but not proven as of 2026-04-14.** possible: the appendix a.2 inspection-principle conditions (pre-registration, composition opacity, fail-closed harness, algebraic independence, inspector pluralism) do not require the operator to be in the oracle seat; they only require that the generator cannot pre-image the composition it is graded against, and that property is compatible with a blind target. not proven: every gp-023 sandbox to date, including sandbox_06, has the operator authoring the ground truth and committing it to the charter. the structural missing piece is the **operator-oracle coupling**, and the cleanest removal is the **blind-oracle pattern**: operator writes a generator-of-generators that samples a non-elementary closed form from a declared family without the operator inspecting the sample; the ztare run happens against the sampled data; the sampled form is revealed only after the run closes and graded post-hoc. sandbox_06 is the calibration precondition for this experiment, not the experiment itself. the discovery test is tracked as h-sp2-04 (merged blind + eml + inversion) in the mission hypothesis ledger. **separately: the tactical vocabulary question — "invert versus eml?" — is a false dichotomy. inversion is the operating system (gates, holdouts, seams, asymptotic standards, fail-closed harness); eml is the atomic vocabulary (removes regression-toolbox comfort bias from the mutator's move set); discovery requires both, composed with a blind target.** `medium / mission-level / honest floor claim` the system has not yet discovered anything without being told the answer first; decisions.source_text: **for a bounded proportion sequence (z(n) = abundant number density), the correct gate normalization is `max_residual / max( z )`, not absolute residual. an absolute threshold of 0.05 on a signal spanning [0.18, 0.25] (range 0.069) is 72% of the signal range — effectively no constraint. using absolute residuals, a maximally wrong form can "pass" by staying within ±0.05 of the signal mean. the fix is normalized residuals with threshold 0.05 (= 5% of the maximum observed signal value).** generalizes to any substrate where the signal range is much smaller than the threshold: normalize by signal magnitude, not absolute value. `high / one substrate / panel-confirmed` normalized residuals are mandatory for bounded proportion signals; check signal range before setting absolute thresholds e-survey-s1-01: absolute harness passed llm champion at 0.048 (correct normalized: 0.193 = fail); panel rejected first harness; corrected harness correctly killed wrong families `projects/survey_s1/gate_harness.py`, e-survey-s1-01

decisions.source_text: **a 3-parameter form `a + b/f(n) + c/n` with unconstrained `a` creates parameter aliasing: `c/n` absorbs the small-n rise while `a` inflates to a biased value (0.2559 vs true ~0.2476), allowing any convergence family to pass the gate. this masks genuine discrimination. the fix: anchor `a` to the analytic asymptote [0.2470, 0.2490]. with `a=0.2476` fixed and `c=0` (single correction term): 1/log(n) fails visible gate (vis_norm=0.248 — b too small to fit steep initial rise), 1/n passes both gates (vis_norm=0.026). conclusion: current evidence at n=50–7000 is better described by 1/n dynamics than 1/log(n) dynamics. the mertens 1/log(n) claim applies at n >> 10^6 and requires the analytic argument, not numerical gates, for support at current scale. gate design rule: always constrain `a` to the theoretically-known asymptote range; unconstrained asymptote + helper correction term = uninformative gate.** `high / confirmed / constrained-fit test` constrain the asymptote parameter using theory before running the gate; unconstrained fitting lets the optimizer inflate `a` and pass any form through aliasing e-survey-s1-02: with a=0.2476 fixed, 1/log(n) fails visible (0.248), 1/n passes (0.026); free-a 3-param forms all pass via inflated a=0.255–0.265 `projects/survey_s1/evidence_farther_tail.txt`, `projects/survey_s1/gate_harness.py`, `projects/survey_s1/thesis.md`

decisions.source_text: **perturbation-invariance testing ("kick the system and check if the same form wins") is a valid methodology for discriminating structural laws from numerical coincidences, but it requires the underlying coefficients to be in their asymptotic regime.** at n≤100k, the b coefficient in `a+b/log(n)` is not stable (drifts by 10× across fitting ranges), so the mertens-predicted coefficient ratio cannot be tested. the perturbation did reveal that the dominant 1/n correction in base data is entangled with even-number composition effects (z_even≈0.492 vs z_odd≈0.004). this is a population-structure artifact, not a structural law. the perturbation harness would become discriminating at n>10^6 where b should stabilize. generalizable: for any sequence with multiplicative structure, perturbation battery (strip small primes) tests whether a correction term is mechanistic or compositional. `medium / methodological / informative null` when coefficients are unstable across fitting ranges, the identification horizon hasn't been reached; extend evidence before claiming structural invariance e-survey-s1-03: b ratio diverges from mertens prediction; winner flip vanishes at n≥5000 `projects/survey_s1/thesis.md`

decisions.source_text: **bimodal phase transition in operator space.** the 28-generator sweep reveals a clean gap in spacing_var: no generator achieves sv between 0.37 and 0.54. phase a (polynomial-dominated): loss 0.26-0.35, sv 0.27-0.37. phase b (arithmetic-dominated): loss 0.63-4.08, sv 0.54-0.65. the gap is empty — the operator space has two structural classes with no interpolant. secondary findings: (1) toeplitz > hankel: st_toeplitz_mangoldt (toeplitz λ( i-j ), loss 0.260) beats st_hankel_mangoldt (hankel λ(i+j), loss 0.305) — translation-invariant coupling outperforms flip-invariant for same arithmetic content. (2) st_n2_gcd shows 74.8% loss drop at restart 6 (1.076 → 0.271), confirming 8 restarts is borderline for basin coverage. decisions.source_text: **dense arithmetic off-diagonal operators (hankel-λ, toeplitz-λ, toeplitz-σ) at n=800 produce no material improvement over polynomial + sparse-arithmetic baselines for matching riemann zeta zero spacings. the polynomial+arithmetic family appears to have a structural ceiling at mse ~0.25 and spacing_var ~0.30, independent of whether arithmetic content is (a) diagonal, (b) sparse off-diagonal (gcd-based), or (c) dense off-diagonal (hankel/toeplitz of λ, σ, τ).** best dense generator (st_toeplitz_mangoldt, loss 0.260) beat best polynomial (st_log2, loss 0.268) by ~3% — within noise. target spacing_var 0.457 was not reached by any generator with reasonable loss. sff-l1 distribution is tight (0.82-1.13) across 28 generators: no generator produces a qualitatively riemann-shaped sff without catastrophic mse. the pareto trade-off between mse-fit and gue-spacing-cv is structural at this n. three consecutive gp-125 runs with distinct grammar classes have confirmed the ceiling: polynomial-confinement (e-gp125-01), sparse off-diagonal arithmetic (riemann off-diagonal 2026-04-23 am), dense off-diagonal arithmetic (this run). **honest next-move options:** (i) scale n_matrix to 2000+ to test whether asymptotic regime breaks the pareto; (ii) abandon real-symmetric operator families entirely and move to complex-hermitian / time-reversal-broken ensembles (goe → gue fix, gp-133 round 3 gemini note); (iii) pivot from riemann-direct to phase-c oeis sky survey (gp-126). option (iii) is the least-compute-per-signal per gp-133 panel recommendations. `confirmed / one n / 28 generator families / three-class grammar coverage` real-symmetric polynomial+arithmetic grammar cannot cross the mse-vs-cv pareto; the structural limit is grammar-class-wide, not within-grammar. supports formal close of the "find hilbert-pólya in polynomial+arithmetic" branch of gp-125. e-gp125-a10-dense-01 per-generator json contains loss / spacing_var / sff_l1 for all 28 families. `projects/riemann_operator_search/workspace/riemann_a10_dense_20260423.json`, cross-ref to e-gp125-01 (gh200 polynomial) and e-tdo-multiseed-01 for the falsify-before-patent discipline pattern
